subject: Intermittent latency spikes — path to stronger uptime guarantees
messages:
From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cartograph.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cartograph.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Latency spikes this week — impact to our ingest pipelines

Irene,

We started seeing intermittent 2–6s tail latency on generation requests Tuesday evening and it impacted a few downstream jobs that rely on fast embeddings/QA responses. The incidents are brief but frequent enough that our ingestion workers back off and retry — overall we saw ~8% throughput degradation across the night window.

We know Cartograph is coming up for renewal in May and this level of variability is a concern for our SRE/Procurement teams. Can you help us understand:
- Do you have a short incident timeline or debug info you can share?
- What options exist for a tighter uptime/latency commitment (SLA tiers, regional affinity, dedicated capacity)?
- Is there a way to pilot a fix that avoids a full contract amendment while we evaluate?

We'd like to schedule a sync with your engineering and commercial leads. Elena and I are available Friday morning PST.

Thanks,
Samir Kapoor
Head of Platform Engineering
Cartograph Analytics

[attachment: incident-timeline.csv]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cartograph.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 10:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spikes this week — impact to our ingest pipelines

Samir —

Thanks for flagging and for the timeline. I'm sorry for the disruption; that level of variability is not what we expect for production workloads. Marcus (runtime) and Grace (customer success) are looped in to triage and propose options.

Quick plan:
1) Marcus will pull traces and a KV-cache hit breakdown and share an interim summary by EOD PST today.
2) We can offer a short pilot of a reserved pool in your primary region (us-west-2) for the critical ingestion routes while we investigate. Pilot would be 2–4 weeks and we can instrument token/latency metrics for visibility.
3) Commercially, we can discuss a temporary SLA credit for the affected window and a path to an upgraded SLA if the pilot demonstrates improved stability.

Would Friday 9:00–9:30am PST work for a quick sync?

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Irene Choi
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0191

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cartograph.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Latency spikes this week — impact to our ingest pipelines

Hi all —

I've pulled logs for the windows Samir included and correlated them with node-level telemetry. High-level findings:
- Root cause appears to be a short-lived resource scheduling contention on a subset of multi-tenant worker pods in us-west-2 during your night batch window. Not a model issue (same model variant across nodes), more of a burst scheduling + kernel CPU saturation on two hosts.
- KV cache hit rates were normal; the extra tail was from occasional context-switch storms when background maintenance (GC/telemetry) coincided with large decodes.

Mitigations we can apply quickly:
- Move your critical routes to a small reserved pool (single-tenant scheduling) — reduces scheduling jitter, consistent CPU allocation.
- Tweak background maintenance windows and token-batching thresholds for your routes.

I'll prepare a short runbook and share the incident snippets; attaching the CSV you provided with annotated timestamps. If you approve, ops can spin up the reserved pool for a 14-day pilot by tomorrow.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

[attachment: incident-timeline.csv]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cartograph.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spikes this week — impact to our ingest pipelines

Samir / Elena —

Thanks for taking the call this morning. Per our discussion, summary and asks:
- Redwood will provision a 14-day reserved pool in us-west-2 for the ingestion routes at no additional charge for the pilot.
- During the pilot we will instrument latency, error-rate, and cost-per-token dashboards and provide a daily digest.
- If the pilot meets a defined stability target (99.9th percentile latency under 1.2s for the ingestion paths) we will provide a commercial path to an SLA amendment for your account (see attached proposed amendment, v1).

What we need from Cartograph:
1) Confirm which routes/paths to pin (list of endpoint names or route IDs).
2) Accept the pilot start date (we can start Mon morning) and agree on success metrics.

Next steps: please reply with route IDs by EOD Monday. I'll kick off the ops request once we have that.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

[attachment: mutual-action-plan.docx]

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cartograph.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cartograph.ai>
Cc: procurement@cartograph.ai, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 17:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spikes this week — impact to our ingest pipelines

Grace / Irene / Aditya —

Quick update from Procurement: we reviewed the proposed amendment and are open to the conditional SLA upgrade if the pilot demonstrates the stability target you outlined. Two procurement items:
- We will need a short-term credit for the night windows impacted (Cartograph reference INC-3341) to make procurement comfortable approving the pilot.
- If the pilot succeeds, procurement requests a 60-day window after pilot close to finalize legal review on the SLA amendment.

Proposed commercial compromise:
- Redwood issues a one-time credit equal to 10% of March spend for the impacted services, applied upon pilot start.
- Pilot runs 14 days, stability target is measured over both night and peak windows.
- If target met, Redwood commits to draft SLA amendment language and Redwood/Cartograph have 60 days to finalize.

We appreciate the fast response and the pilot offer — please confirm and we'll route procurement approval.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
VP, Finance & Ops
Cartograph Analytics
